title: FIFA cyberattack and data theft, Nov 2026

subject.name: FIFA
subject.about: FIFA, the Fédération Internationale de Football Association, has been the global governing body for football since 1904. It sets the rules of the game, works with 211 member associations and organises tournaments such as the FIFA World Cup.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by FIFA, any football body, any news outlet, company, group, or anyone else named.
size_basis: FIFA is football's world governing body. What is known: it says a limited set of personal and business information was accessed. It has given no count of people affected, so the reach is not known.
who_is_affected: People and organisations whose information FIFA holds; FIFA has not said who. Nothing it has said mentions fans or ticket holders. FIFA has asked no one to take any action.

known.text: FIFA says a criminal cyberattack gave someone unauthorised access to a limited set of personal and business information.
FIFA says it is working with the authorities, including law enforcement.
FIFA has not said how many people were affected, when the attack happened or what the information was.

not_known.text: Who carried out the attack. A group says it did; FIFA has not said.
Whose information was accessed, and whether fans or ticket holders are among them.
How much data was taken. FIFA has given no figure.

figures.label: Data the group claims it stole
figures.detail: The group's claim; FIFA has not confirmed it
